text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A political row is brewing over pensions, in most cases higher for men than women. The trade ministry and leading pension funds see no need for change but opposition parties are pressing for legislation to outlaw discrimination.
--- So far only the Danish state has profitted from the 1990 establishment of the first casinos in Denmark, through large gambling taxes.

--- A new OECD report places Denmark with among others Portugal and Turkey as one of 21 industrial countries with the lowest educational level for people between the age of 25 and 34, shaking the idea that Danes have one of the higest levels of education in the world.

--- Western Europe's worst dressed group of people - Danish men - appear to have been better dressed in 1996 with increased clothes purchases, while Danish women did not increase clothes purchases. Clothing retailers total turnover increased by 3.6 percent in the first ten months of 1996 compared to the same period of 1995.
--- A new survey shows that more than 50 percent of Danish voters do not want to change Denmark's optouts on EMU, military cooperation or European Union citizenship.
